name: Tesla
description: Tesla sells electric vehicles (Model 3, Y, S, X, Cybertruck, Semi), energy storage (Megapack for utilities, Powerwall for homes) and solar, plus services: used cars, charging, insurance, parts, and Full Self-Driving software subscriptions. In FY2025 vehicle deliveries fell 9% to about 1.63M and automotive revenue fell 10% to $69.5B, but energy storage revenue rose 27% to $12.8B on 46.7 GWh deployed (+49%). Operating income fell 38% to $4.4B. Regulatory credits sold to other automakers (down 28% to $2.0B) were about 46% of that profit. The company is investing in a robotaxi service (launched June 2025), Cybercab, Optimus humanoid robots, and its own lithium refinery (running January 2026), while US consumer EV tax credits were repealed by the July 4, 2025 law.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass.

businessLines.name: Automotive (sales, leasing, regulatory credits)
businessLines.how: One-time vehicle sales and some leases to consumers and fleets, plus regulatory credits sold to other automakers to meet emission rules ($1,993M FY2025, -28%); FSD software sold or subscribed sits in this line or services (not split in the sources read).

businessLines.name: Energy generation and storage
businessLines.how: Sells Megapack grid batteries mostly to utilities and developers on multi-month project contracts, plus Powerwall home batteries and solar; lumpy by project deliveries.

businessLines.name: Services and other
businessLines.how: Used vehicles, Supercharging, insurance, parts and repair, merchandise; recurring but small margin.

brands.name: Model 3 / Model Y
brands.note: Volume cars; model-level deliveries not extracted

whatsNext.text: Six new production lines (vehicle, Bots, energy storage, battery) ramping in 2026; Cortex 2 AI training cluster under construction at Gigafactory Texas
In-house lithium refinery in Texas began operations January 2026
